audit.whatIsWrong: Every row of the chart said Sett, including the rows whose own captions hand the window to Kayle (whys[4] 'neither side cleanly owns', whys[5]/[6] describe you kiting and melting him).
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Sett,Sett,Sett,Sett,Skill,Kayle,Kayle and the 54.47% win rate over 727 games matches a scaling flip, not a Sett-owned 2-item window.
audit.corrected: Rows 4-6 flipped to Skill/Kayle/Kayle in both layers with ratings to match.

audit.why: Level 6 (Divine Ascent range + Divine Judgment), Nashor's, and 2+ items are the right spikes; Sett's are Haymaker online and level 6.

audit.whatIsWrong: Text claimed Pit Grit 'crits every other auto on the same target', called The Show Stopper a suppress, and treated Facebreaker as an unconditional grab-stun. Packet also flags that no Sett ability was ever named.
audit.why: Riot text: Pit Grit alternates left and right punch, the right being slightly stronger and faster — no crit. Facebreaker pulls enemies on opposite sides and stuns them; with enemies on one side only they are slowed instead. The Show Stopper is a carry-and-slam with a slow, not a suppression, and it grounds.
audit.corrected: Real names used throughout, the crit claim removed, and Facebreaker's both-sides condition stated as the defensive rule — keep the wave behind you and his stun is a slow.

audit.whatIsWrong: No concrete cooldown numbers on the matchup-defining ability.
audit.why: Haymaker is 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s and Facebreaker 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s — both long enough to step up on.
audit.corrected: Haymaker's 18s rank-1 cooldown added to the do's.

edits.before: His level-3 E grab-stun into a fully-charged W true-damage smash can all-in you outright — stay out of E range and just farm.
edits.after: Facebreaker stuns only with enemies on both sides of him — keep the minions behind you and his level-3 all-in is a slow, not a stun.

edits.before: Sett's window: alternating-fist passive (every other auto crits the same target) plus a fully-charged W true-damage smash shred you while you're a melee Kayle with only a point in Q (Radiant Blast) and no escape.
edits.after: Sett's window: Pit Grit alternates fists and the right punch lands harder and faster, and stored Grit gives Haymaker a true-damage core, while you are melee with one point in Q (Radiant Blast) and no escape.

edits.before: Divine Ascent's ranged form comes online and Divine Judgment (R) gives you a few seconds of invulnerability, so his charged-W smash and R suppress can no longer just delete you and the lane stabilizes.
edits.after: Divine Ascent's ranged form comes online and Divine Judgment (R) gives you a few seconds of invulnerability, so a charged Haymaker and The Show Stopper can no longer just delete you and the lane stabilizes.

edits.before: Levels 1-5 are Sett's and you have to concede them: he out-grits you in every short trade because his passive crits every other auto on the same target and his W charges true damage off the punishment he eats, while you're a melee Kayle with only Q (Radiant Blast) and no escape. The thing that kills you is E grab-stun into a fully-charged W smash, so never walk into his E range to contest a wave — last-hit at the very tip of Q for the armor/MR shred and slow, and give up CS rather than feed his W charge by trading back when you can't win.
edits.after: Levels 1-5 are Sett's and you have to concede them: he out-grits you in every short trade because Pit Grit's right punch lands harder and faster and Haymaker charges true damage off the punishment he eats, while you're a melee Kayle with only Q (Radiant Blast) and no escape. What kills you is Facebreaker into a charged Haymaker — but it stuns only with enemies on both sides of him, so keep the wave behind you and it is just a slow. Last-hit at the tip of Q for the resistance shred, and give up CS rather than feeding his Grit.

edits.before: Level 6 is your first breath: once Divine Ascent's stacks convert, your autos go ranged with AoE magic waves and Divine Judgment (R) buys you a few seconds of full invulnerability, so his charged-W smash and R suppress can no longer simply delete you and the lane settles toward even. Don't get greedy — he can still E-grab you if you hug him and his level-6 all-in is real. Hold spacing with W (Celestial Blessing) move speed, chip with ranged E (Starfire) missing-health on-hits, and save R to eat his Show Stopper if he commits. Once Nashor's lands you start out-DPSing his grit from outside E range.
edits.after: Level 6 is your first breath: once Divine Ascent's stacks convert, your autos go ranged with AoE magic waves and Divine Judgment (R) buys you a few seconds of full invulnerability, so a charged Haymaker and his slam can no longer simply delete you and the lane settles toward even. Don't get greedy — Facebreaker still reaches 490 units and his level-6 all-in is real. Hold spacing with W (Celestial Blessing) move speed, chip with ranged E (Starfire) missing-health on-hits, and save R for The Show Stopper if he commits. Once Nashor's lands you out-DPS his Grit from outside his range.

edits.before: Land E grab-stun into a fully-charged W true-damage smash to all-in you before level 6
edits.after: Catch you with minions on his far side so Facebreaker stuns, then dump a charged Haymaker

edits.before: Use the alternating-fist passive and stored W damage to win every short trade while you're melee-locked
edits.after: Land Knuckle Down's max-health punches and stored Haymaker Grit to win every short trade while you're melee

edits.before: Hit his level-6 R suppress on you while you're still melee and your stacks/R aren't enough to escape
edits.after: Land The Show Stopper on you while you're still melee and your stacks and R can't cover the slam

edits.before: Shield + true damage. Dodge it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Shield plus a true-damage core, 18s at rank 1 — bait it, then step up.

notes: Pit Grit does not crit — it alternates punches with a stronger, faster right. Facebreaker stuns only when enemies are on opposite sides of Sett; alone against him with the wave behind you it is a slow, which is the single most useful fact in this lane. The Show Stopper is a carry-slam with a slow and grounding, not a suppression.
